title: C1673 — Fuel Injection Pump
introduction:
The title identifies the fuel injection pump; the circuit table gets more specific by naming the fuel-volume-regulator connection and its return. I use the drawing’s cavity labels to reach those rows, then follow the parts tables separately. It is a small electrical address book for the pump—each entry has a particular job.

This guide covers connector-reference reading. Access, electrical testing, replacement and opening fuel plumbing require their own procedures. Physical viewing side, test conditions, gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used are unspecified here; no engine application is assigned.

edits.why: I use the vertically stacked cavity labels, stepped inner outline and broad rectangular feature on the drawing’s right to navigate this face illustration. The table beneath connects the drawing to its Fpn and harness entry. Read these alongside the identification table to keep the pump connector’s identity attached to the correct map.

Follow each drawn cavity label to its matching Cavity row, then read horizontally through the circuit and wire fields. Function distinguishes the fuel-volume-regulator return from the fuel-volume-regulator connection, both associated with the powertrain controller. I keep the return designation intact rather than treating it as a general chassis-ground label. Terminal Part Number identifies the contact part separately from Circuit Number.

Kit List connects the identification table to Number in the pigtail listing. I read Service Part as the service reference and use Engineering Shell to connect that row back to Hard Shell and Fpn. Gauge, Material and Cavities describe the pigtail entry; Image names the associated illustration file. This separates the assembly reference from the shell and individual terminal references.

Product Id provides a separate European pigtail reference. I keep it with its regional heading when recording the listing. Its presence alongside the other service-parts table does not by itself establish interchangeability or application coverage.
